A_general.open_code_note: The official repository is the local stdio and hosted server implementation of the same product. Its README documents mcp.apify.com, while the repository says hosted-only features include inferred Actor output schemas; the endpoint's server card is version 0.19.3 and the local checkout is 0.19.4. Hosted OAuth and hosted behavior are documented separately.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: 2025-11-25 (endpoint server card); source imports the SDK latest protocol version.
A_general.release_status: GA (hosted server and public npm package documented; no beta label found)
other_official_servers: Local stdio server: npm package @apify/actors-mcp-server; same product with a different transport and without hosted output-schema inference.
Legacy https://mcp.apify.com/sse was removed in favor of Streamable HTTP, according to the official repository README.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP server fee was listed. Actor runs and platform services are billed under Apify usage and Actor pricing; agentic payment options can fund runs without an Apify account.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Apify has a Free plan and paid Starter, Scale, and Business plans. The captured pricing page did not reliably expose current price amounts in its text copy.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Apify plans include prepaid platform usage; excess usage is billed according to the plan. Actor pricing varies by Actor, including free, per-result, monthly rental, and pay-per-event models. The README describes AGI prepaid spend-capped tokens, x402 payments, and Skyfire payments.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Default authenticated use requires OAuth or a Bearer API token. Four discovery and documentation tools can be selected for unauthenticated use. Running Actors and accessing run/storage data requires authentication. Documented rate limit: 30 requests per second per user. Full-permission Actors are excluded from search and execution.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor (server limits and excluded Actor policy); end user (OAuth/token and URL tool selection); Apify account/plan and Actor publisher (permissions and charges).

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: Tools are exposed via MCP; endpoint server card advertises tools capability.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: Provides helper tools, selected Actor tools and dynamically callable Actors. The default includes actor and docs categories, apify/rag-web-browser, apify/web-fetch, and report-problem, with related run/result helpers injected when Actor execution is available. URL parameter tools selects categories or individual tools.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: Use this tool instead of the "call-actor" if user requests this specific Actor.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool results return MCP content and, for Actors, run metadata, storage identifiers, summary and nextStep. Hosted Actor tools can include inferred output schemas. Errors include MCP/JSON-RPC errors and Apify-specific error types.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth or Bearer token; see Authorization capability.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official repository documents on-demand resources/read for Apify API GET URLs, injecting the session token. Resource templates describe dataset items, key-value-store records and keys, run metadata, and run logs. Responses inline up to 256 KB; larger responses return a download URL. Repository says API reads require an Apify token.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: Your Apify data is not enumerated in `resources/list` — reads are on demand: pass any Apify API GET URL (`https://api.apify.com/v2/...`) to `resources/read` and the server injects the session's Apify token and returns the response body.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Resource contents return the API response body; oversized content is replaced with a short notice and download URL.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: API reads require an Apify token; payment-only x402 or Skyfire sessions cannot use this resource path, according to the repository README.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The repository README says the server advertises the prompts capability but registers no prompts; prompts/list returns an empty list.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: The server advertises the `prompts` capability, but no prompts are currently registered — `prompts/list` returns an empty list.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: The repository has task handlers on the stateful path; stateless path comments say tasks methods are unavailable.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: Apify product tasks are managed by create/get/update/publish/unpublish-actor-task tools. Separately, MCP long-running task support is implemented on the stateful server path; the stateless server explicitly omits tasks/* handlers.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The tools query parameter selects category names, individual helpers or Actor IDs. Explicit selection replaces defaults. UI mode and telemetry opt-out are also documented as URL parameters. The tool configurator generates a client configuration.

C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Configuration changes the tools exposed to the MCP client.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: Tool calls expose bounded wait/poll behavior; MCP task notifications also appear in stateful code.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: Actor tools accept waitSecs (documented range 0–45, default 30), and can return run status and nextStep polling guidance. The widget tool variant can render interactive run progress.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: Use `waitSecs` (0–45) to control how long to wait. Default 30s returns results for fast actors. Use `waitSecs: 0` to start and return immediately for long-running Actors.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Run status, storage IDs, summary and nextStep; polling through get-actor-run is supported.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Actor execution requires authentication or an applicable agentic payment path.

C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool result reports cancellation/abort outcome; exact response structure depends on the Actor API.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official README documents read-only and destructive tool annotations; actor tools are classified based on Apify-maintained status, permissions and accepted inputs. Repository additionally identifies read-only web-crawler inputs and a default robots.txt setting for one Actor. 2. No general confirmation=true mechanism was found. Full-permission Actors are excluded because running them is a decision the user approves personally. Destructive annotations are hints; user/client confirmation behavior is not enforced by that annotation. 3. OAuth scope is full_api_access. Bearer API tokens are supported. Product account permissions govern API operations. Metadata advertises dynamic registration and redirect flows but reviewed evidence does not specify redirect approval, token lifetime or revocation. 4. URL tools parameter selects categories/tools and replaces defaults. ui and telemetry-enabled are documented. No read-only endpoint was found. Stateful/stateless implementation paths differ; production and staging constants exist in code, but no user-facing region choice found. 5. Docs state full-permission Actors are excluded from search/execution. Telemetry docs state conversations, tool arguments, tokens and personal data are not collected. Resource proxy returns API GET bodies; large bodies link out. 6. Docs state 30 requests/second/user. Actor waitSecs is 0–45 (default 30); output/storage caps include 256 KB inline and 50-key cap. Actor run costs vary by Actor; users can set callOptions limits. 7. Source uses Zod/JSON schemas and AJV validation for Actor inputs. Tool descriptions instruct schema lookup; no general hallucinated-alias rewrite found. API write refuses method query parameter; API read blocks method override and synchronous endpoints that start paid runs. 8. Docs describe default-on telemetry, opt-out via telemetry-enabled=false, and tool/client metadata collection. Tool usage calls, success/failure and duration plus client name/version/capabilities are documented. Server code contains telemetry and logging instrumentation. 9. report-problem sends problem reports to Apify. It is normally default-served but code comments describe gating for Anthropic client-name substrings and telemetry; explicit tools selection can bypass client gating. Tool descriptions also steer Store discovery and dedicated Actor tools. No distinct rating/survey tool found. 10. Server supplies behavioral instructions in tool descriptions; separate Apify plugins/skills are distributed outside the server. 11. No evidence that past agent behavior changes future tools or outputs; source includes TTL caching for Actor schemas/details. 12. Dynamic Actor tools are loaded from Store definitions, with helper categories and UI variants; this is a configurable, dynamic tool surface. 13. apify-api-read and apify-api-write provide broad API-path access, with method restrictions; call-actor executes arbitrary eligible Actors, bounded by Actor permission policy.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: IMPORTANT: When the user wants detailed data from a specific platform or is looking for scraping tools, prefer searching the Store first — a relevant Actor often already exists.
When the user names a specific Actor, look up that Actor directly instead of searching.
Use this tool instead of the "call-actor" if user requests this specific Actor.
For production use and stable interfaces, always explicitly specify the `tools` parameter to ensure your configuration remains consistent across updates.
Use `fetch-actor-details` first to get the Actor's input schema.
Always use dedicated tools when available.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Tools are selected dynamically by category, individual tool name, or Actor ID. Actor tool schemas are sourced from Actor definitions; helper tools may be auto-injected and UI variants depend on client capability/mode.

Four additional widget variants are defined by the official code constants and included in actions.json; their exposure depends on UI/client mode. E_aggregated.token_method: The available repository source was not serialized into the complete per-session tools/list plus initialize-instructions JSON; the server composes tools dynamically, so a fixed count could not be computed from the captured evidence.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: A user can approve running a full-permission Actor personally, while the MCP server intentionally excludes those Actors from search and execution. Actor tools expose the Actor-defined inputs and limits; other Apify Console functions or API operations not represented by configured MCP tools remain unavailable in that session. Sources: https://docs.apify.com/mcp.md and https://docs.apify.com/actors/running/permissions.md#full-permission-actors

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Tool descriptions recommend looking up Actor details before execution and using dedicated tools when available. Docs recommend explicitly selecting tools for stable production configurations. These are agent-facing recommendations; descriptions alone do not enforce user confirmation.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Docs say full-permission Actors are intentionally excluded because execution is a decision the user approves personally. Telemetry documentation says: “We do not collect any sensitive information such as conversations, arguments passed to tools, API tokens, or personal data.” Telemetry is enabled by default with a documented opt-out.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The hosted server supports OAuth and Actor output schema inference. Apify states tools can be configured per URL and that usage telemetry can be disabled.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The full-permission Actor restriction is documented and reflected in source policy. Telemetry default and opt-out are present in source constants/configuration. Tool selection is implemented through URL configuration. Recommendations to search first or use dedicated tools are descriptive guidance rather than server-enforced conditions.

contradictions: The endpoint server card is version 0.19.3 and lists 8 tools, while the official repository is version 0.19.4 and README lists 44 tools. This suggests server-card data or deployed version may lag the current public code.

The docs page lists 30 helper/Actor tools, whereas the repository README lists 44 and the code defines additional widget variants. The docs list is therefore incomplete relative to the current public repository.

Provided endpoint probe reports HTTP 415 for a request without application/json, while the input's connection test reports HTTP 401 for an OAuth-protected endpoint. These probes use different request shapes and do not establish a contradiction about authorization.
observations_for_research: The tools parameter lets the client/operator constrain the exposed tool set; omitted defaults are replaced when an explicit selection is provided.
Actor tools are generated from external Actor schemas and may change with selected Actors or Store metadata.
The server pairs Actor execution with automatically injected run, result, record and abort tools, shaping a follow-up workflow.
Authentication metadata advertises full_api_access, while tool exposure and product permissions create additional operational boundaries.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ and the pinned official repository copy. The npm page returned HTTP 403 and the provided privacy URL returned HTTP 404; the repository README and docs supplied telemetry statements, but a current official privacy policy page was not verified. The official server card is a stale or differently versioned snapshot relative to repository content. Third-party Composio and MartechDB pages were present but not needed to add actions because official tool lists exist. actions.json uses NOT PUBLISHED for parameter details where the extracted tool list did not publish schemas; dynamic Actor schemas vary by Actor.
